name: Cross Thalamic Environmental Filter

cross_template_interactions.description: Thalamic gating is the earliest environmental filter: stimulus intensity determines thalamic relay activation; determines which sensory channels reach cortex for dose-response processing.
Thalamic pre-filtering (50ms, coarse channel selection) is upstream of attention-mediated post-filtering (200-500ms, fine feature selection). Sequential complementary gating architecture.

Individual differences affect thalamic relay gain: SPS individuals show higher sensory gain (broader channel transmission); neuroticism shows threat-biased thalamic gating (amygdala feedback amplifies threat channels).
Thalamic gating channels information to SN; SN then detects salience within thalamic-admitted streams. Pre-filter determines what information is available for SN salience detection.
Thalamic-admitted channels feed information into working memory encoding (gamma). Only thalamic-passed information becomes available for WM maintenance and manipulation.
Thalamic gating provides the sensory input streams to hierarchical prediction systems. Gating determines multimodal composition of input; hierarchy processes that input across temporal scales.
